_source: Advanced urban systems taxonomy for climate adaptation. Multi-tiered hierarchy mapping physical, ecological, and socio-economic urban subsystems.
_note: This taxonomy enables precise classification of where a solution is deployed and what it protects. Supports interdependency analysis and critical bottleneck identification. v0.1.1: added informal_service_systems subsector under socioeconomic_health to capture service provision filled by informal actors where formal systems are absent — addresses IPCC AR6 Ch. 6 critique that ISO 37120 misses informal urban systems entirely. v1.2: every system has a definition. Rule: an urban system is something a city has whether or not it adapts; a thing that is itself an intervention is a Solution. Ten terms are retired (status: deprecated, replaced_by: the systems to use instead; an empty list means none). Sector ids may be used as system_id for sector-level links.

sectors.name: Built Environment & Land Use
sectors.description: Physical structures and spatial zoning. Solutions involve retrofitting, managed retreat, or building code changes.

systems.name: High-Density / Multi-Family
systems.definition: Multi-family housing: apartment blocks, high-rises and dense row housing.

systems.name: Low-Density / Single-Family
systems.definition: Single-family and other low-density housing, typical of suburbs.

systems.name: Informal Settlements / Slums
systems.examples: Highly vulnerable areas lacking formal infrastructure
systems.definition: Housing built without formal tenure, planning or services.

systems.name: Central Business Districts (CBDs)
systems.definition: Downtown commercial cores and dense office districts.

systems.name: Heavy Industry / Manufacturing
systems.definition: Factories, industrial parks and manufacturing plants.

systems.name: Logistics & Warehousing
systems.definition: Distribution centres, warehouses and storage facilities.

systems.name: Healthcare Facilities
systems.definition: Hospitals, clinics and other buildings where health care is delivered.

systems.name: Educational Facilities
systems.definition: Schools, colleges and universities.

systems.name: Government & Emergency Response
systems.examples: Municipal buildings, fire stations, police stations, EOCs
systems.definition: Public buildings for government and emergency services: city halls, fire and police stations, emergency operations centres, and the shelters and warning operations run from them.

systems.name: Cultural Heritage Sites
systems.definition: Historic buildings, monuments, archaeological sites and cultural landscapes.

systems.name: Floodplains & Low-Lying Coastal Zones
systems.definition: Low-lying land in river floodplains and along the coast, including its shorelines, riverbanks and flood defences.

systems.name: Steep Slopes
systems.definition: Hillsides and slopes prone to landslides and erosion.

systems.name: Brownfields & Reclaimed Land
systems.definition: Former industrial land, landfills and reclaimed sites.

systems.name: Subsurface Space
systems.definition: Underground space: basements, underground parking, utility vaults and tunnels.

sectors.name: Mobility & Transport Networks
sectors.description: Systems for moving people and goods. Solutions maintain flow during extreme events and prevent material degradation.

systems.name: Arterial Roads & Highways
systems.definition: Major roads, highways and expressways.

systems.name: Local/Municipal Street Networks
systems.definition: Neighbourhood and collector streets, including their sidewalks, parking and right-of-way.

systems.name: Bridges, Tunnels, and Viaducts
systems.definition: Bridges, tunnels and viaducts.

systems.name: Active Mobility Networks
systems.definition: Walking and cycling infrastructure: paths, bike lanes and greenway trails.

systems.name: Rail Networks
systems.definition: Subway, light rail and commuter rail lines.

systems.name: Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) & Surface Bus
systems.definition: Bus networks, bus lanes and bus rapid transit.

systems.name: Transit Nodes
systems.definition: Stations, terminals, depots and maintenance yards.

systems.name: Maritime Ports & Harbors
systems.examples: Seaports highly exposed to sea-level rise
systems.definition: Seaports and harbours.

systems.name: Airports
systems.definition: Runways, terminals and airport facilities.

systems.name: Freight Rail Yards
systems.definition: Freight rail lines and cargo yards.

sectors.name: Hydrological & Water Infrastructure
sectors.description: Water sourcing, distribution, and management. Most heavily impacted by climate change.

systems.name: Source Water
systems.definition: Where drinking water comes from: reservoirs, aquifers, rivers and catchments.

systems.name: Treatment Facilities
systems.examples: Desalination plants, purification centers, water treatment plants
systems.definition: Plants that make water safe to drink, including desalination.

systems.name: Distribution Networks
systems.examples: Pumping stations, water mains, storage tanks
systems.definition: Pumping stations, mains and storage that carry treated water to users.

systems.name: Collection Networks
systems.definition: Storm sewers and combined sewers that collect runoff.

systems.name: Outfalls & Discharge Points
systems.definition: Points where stormwater or combined sewage discharges to a water body.

systems.name: Surface Conveyance
systems.definition: Open drainage that carries runoff on the surface: channels, ditches, culverts and swales.

systems.name: Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTPs)
systems.definition: Plants that treat sewage.

systems.name: Sanitary Sewer Networks
systems.definition: Pipes that carry sewage to treatment.

systems.name: Decentralized Sanitation
systems.definition: On-site and local sanitation: septic systems and small treatment units.

systems.name: Solid Waste Management
systems.definition: Formal collection, transfer, recycling and disposal of solid waste, including landfills. Use informal_solid_waste for waste pickers and informal recycling.

systems.name: Hard Engineering
systems.definition: Retired in v1.2: seawalls, levees and barrages are Solutions, not urban systems. Link them to the floodplain, shoreline or waterway they protect.

systems.name: Managed Waterways
systems.examples: Canals, dredged channels, flood control structures
systems.definition: Engineered waterways and their control structures: canals, dredged channels, pumping stations and flood gates.

sectors.name: Energy & Telecommunications
sectors.description: The nervous system. Solutions prevent cascading failures from flooded substations affecting hospitals and communications.

systems.name: Centralized Power Plants
systems.definition: Large power plants: fossil, nuclear and large hydro.

systems.name: Decentralized / Distributed Generation
systems.definition: Small-scale generation near users: rooftop solar, small turbines and combined heat and power.

systems.name: District Heating & Cooling
systems.definition: Networks that distribute heating or cooling from a central plant.

systems.name: High-Voltage Transmission
systems.definition: High-voltage transmission lines and towers.

systems.name: Substations & Transformers
systems.definition: Substations and transformers.

systems.name: Local Grid / Last-Mile Distribution
systems.definition: Low-voltage distribution lines and cables to buildings.

systems.name: Energy Storage
systems.definition: Grid-scale storage such as batteries and pumped hydro.

systems.name: Data Centers
systems.definition: Facilities that house servers and network equipment.

systems.name: Physical Networks
systems.definition: Fibre and cable networks for telecommunications.

systems.name: Wireless Networks
systems.definition: Cell towers, radio repeaters and other wireless infrastructure.

sectors.name: Urban Ecology & Natural Capital
sectors.description: Urban nature as functional infrastructure providing ecosystem services (cooling, water retention).

systems.name: Public Parks & Plazas
systems.definition: Public parks, squares and recreational open space.

systems.name: Streetscapes & Urban Canopies
systems.definition: Street trees and planting along streets, and the tree canopy they form.

systems.name: Institutional Grounds
systems.definition: Landscaped grounds of campuses, cemeteries and golf courses.

systems.name: Constructed Wetlands & Bioswales
systems.definition: Retired in v1.2: constructed wetlands and bioswales are Solutions, not urban systems. Link them to the drainage or riparian system they serve.

systems.name: Permeable Surfaces
systems.definition: Retired in v1.2: permeable paving is a Solution, not an urban system. Link it to the streets, parks or drainage it is built in.

systems.name: Green Roofs & Vertical Gardens
systems.definition: Retired in v1.2: a green roof is a Solution, not an urban system. Link it to the building system it sits on.

systems.name: Urban Forests & Greenbelts
systems.definition: Woodlands, greenbelts and protected natural areas in and around the city.

systems.name: Coastal Buffers
systems.definition: Natural coastal ecosystems that buffer the shore: mangroves, salt marshes, dunes and reefs.

systems.name: Riparian Zones
systems.definition: Land and vegetation along rivers and streams.

sectors.name: Socio-Economic & Public Health Systems
sectors.description: Operational and social systems. Solutions include early warning systems, cooling centers, and community networks.

systems.name: Vulnerable Population Demographics
systems.definition: Retired in v1.2: a population group, not an urban system. Use ExposureUnit.affected_group or Action.target_populations.

systems.name: Vector-Borne Disease Monitoring
systems.definition: Retired in v1.2: disease surveillance is a Solution, not an urban system. Link it to public_health_services.

systems.name: Emergency Medical Services (EMS)
systems.definition: Ambulance services and first responders.

systems.name: Public Health Services
systems.examples: Health departments, disease surveillance, vector control
systems.definition: Public health functions of the city: health departments, disease surveillance, vector control and health programmes.

systems.name: Local Supply Chains
systems.definition: The networks that supply food and essential goods to the city.

systems.name: Retail & Service Sectors
systems.definition: Shops, services and local businesses.

systems.name: Informal Economies
systems.examples: Street vendors, unregistered labor - highly vulnerable
systems.definition: Unregistered work and trade, such as street vending and day labour.

systems.name: Community Networks & NGOs
systems.definition: Community organisations, civic groups, NGOs and the social ties between residents, including the community facilities they run.

systems.name: Resilience Hubs
systems.examples: Community centers equipped for off-grid survival
systems.definition: Retired in v1.2: a resilience hub is a Solution, not an urban system. Link it to the community or emergency system it serves.

subsectors.name: Informal Service Systems
subsectors._note: Service provision filled by informal actors and arrangements where formal systems are absent, insufficient, or inaccessible. Critical for modeling adaptation in cities of the Global South per IPCC AR6 Ch. 6, which observes that ISO 37120 and similar formal taxonomies miss these systems even when they serve a majority of residents.

systems.name: Informal Water Supply
systems.examples: Water vendors, tanker trucks, private boreholes serving communities without piped supply
systems.definition: Water from vendors, tankers and private boreholes where there is no piped supply.

systems.name: Informal Sanitation
systems.examples: Pit latrines, manual desludging services, decentralized community toilets
systems.definition: Pit latrines, manual emptying and shared community toilets.

systems.name: Informal Solid Waste & Recycling
systems.examples: Waste pickers, informal recyclers, neighborhood collection arrangements
systems.definition: Waste pickers, informal recyclers and neighbourhood collection arrangements.

systems.name: Informal Transport
systems.examples: Paratransit, jitneys, motorcycle taxis, informal minibus networks
systems.definition: Paratransit: minibuses, jitneys and motorcycle taxis.

systems.name: Informal Energy Provision
systems.examples: Unmetered grid connections, charcoal/biomass markets, shared generators
systems.definition: Unmetered connections, charcoal and biomass markets, and shared generators.

systems.name: Community-Led Disaster Response
systems.examples: Mutual aid networks, neighborhood watch, volunteer evacuation coordination, faith-based response
systems.definition: Mutual aid, volunteer and faith-based networks that respond to disasters.

systems.name: Informal Food Systems
systems.examples: Street vendors, wet markets, urban subsistence agriculture, mutual food banks
systems.definition: Street food, wet markets, subsistence farming and community food banks.

sectors.name: Governance, Policy & Finance
sectors.description: Rules of the game. Many adaptation solutions are purely administrative or financial interventions.

systems.name: Building Codes & Standards
systems.definition: The rules that govern how buildings are designed and built.

systems.name: Zoning & Spatial Planning
systems.definition: Land-use rules and the planning system that controls development.

systems.name: Municipal Finance
systems.examples: Green bonds, resilience budgets, climate funds
systems.definition: The city's budget, revenues, debt and reserves.

systems.name: Insurance Markets
systems.definition: Retired in v1.2: climate insurance is a Solution. Link insurance-related actions to municipal_finance.

systems.name: Early Warning Systems (EWS)
systems.definition: Retired in v1.2: an early-warning system is a Solution, not an urban system. Link it to the emergency services it supports.

systems.name: Evacuation & Sheltering
systems.definition: Retired in v1.2: evacuation and sheltering are Solutions, not urban systems. Link them to the emergency services or buildings involved.

sectors.name: Agriculture & Food Systems
sectors.description: Climate adaptation actions focused on agricultural practices, crop management, livestock improvement, paludiculture, and food production systems. Includes technological interventions (crop varieties, genetic techniques), behavioral changes (cropping practices, agroecology), and agricultural extension services.

sectors.name: Emergency & Disaster Management
sectors.description: Actions focused on disaster planning, preparedness, emergency response protocols, and scenario exercises for climate-related hazards. Distinct from general governance by emphasizing operational readiness and emergency coordination.
